plan: Full experiment design delivered in nine sections per the researcher's outline: (1) Objective & Hypotheses including pre-registered H0/H1/H1a/H1b; (2) Simulated workload and schedulers (CPU discrete-event simulator, stdlib-only, 6 schedules); (3) Activation rule and configuration matrix (k*p selector, assumed) plus argument matrix; (4) Sweep design with formal global bubble rate (= Sum_s idle_s / (p * T_steady)), per-stage secondary metric, formal steady-state window from first backward dispatch of last MB at stage 0 to last backward completion, pre-registered 1% threshold with justification tied to comm-floor and 1F1B classical anchor, discrete grid (p in {2,4,8,16}, M in {2..32}(p-1), r=c_W/c_B in {0.5,1,2}, comm in {0,low,high}); (5) Controls/comparators ZB-H1/H2 plus GPipe, 1F1B, Interleaved 1F1B; (6) Seven internal-validity checks including the 1F1B (p-1)/M anchor and the ZB-2p monotonicity-in-M anchor; (7) Analysis plan with tables A-D, plots 1-4, 95% bootstrap CIs over cost-noise draws, 95% cell-pass criterion for H1, asymptotic 1/M-extrapolation intercept; (8) Feasibility/limitations including simulator scope, GPU confounding not reproduced, computational budget of <10 min on 24 cores, and explicit upgrade path; (9) Carried-forward assumptions and open uncertainties. Design-only; no experiment has been executed; all schedule-wiring details and flag-to-schedule mappings explicitly flagged as assumed where source verification is impossible in this workspace.

context.question: Does the automatic scheduling algorithm’s output (ZB-2p) truly achieve a near-zero bubble rate in practice when profiled on multiple GPUs? (Note: The ZB-2p schedule should be activated by setting the appropriate zero bubble configuration flag, for example --zero-bubble-max-pending-backward set to twice the number of pipeline stages.)
